title: Why New York bands needed arrangements; drums and guitar
summary: Harlem audiences wanted variety beyond the Blues, with West Indians, Puerto Ricans and Cubans in the mix; trap drummer and guitar traditions.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Yeah. And we also are speaking about bands that, when they came to New York, their music changed, and they had to get arrangements with much more variations than the Blues, you know -- more kind of things. Here you had bands like Don Redman, Benny Carter, Teddy Hill, Fletcher Henderson, and these bands had arrangements of all types. Because I mean, for you to be playing the Blues all night, it wasn't really compatible with the Eastern...with Harlemites, I would say. They wanted to hear other things, too, you know. I don't think you had many West Indians in Kansas City, Puerto Ricans or Cubans... Or in St. Louis or Alabama.
You follow what I'm saying? They don't get... They don't have that there.
There are West Indians, there are Jamaicans, and you know, from all the different islands -- they had all kind of people here, you know. So therefore, you're jumping into the pot.
Over there, of course, out in the West, as far as the rhythmic sound, you always had the Indians. They were saying something in their day, because...
Just a minute. Let me get finished. I mean, a drummer... When you asked for a drummer in New York, say, for instance... In those days you said a trap drummer, right?

Well, he would bring his drums, bass drum, his glockenspiel maybe, a whistle, a triangle, a railroad bell (heh-heh) and a tom-tom! So you had the whole kind... You were ready to imitate all kinds of sounds.

But I'm just saying... In the South, I guess... The guitar was being played, too, you know, because the Blues players played guitar, and then besides, the banjo... The banjo was more tuned I guess more to country sounds. But when it came to playing the real home-down blues and all that, you had to grab that guitar and slide down that string and all that, and make that bluesy sound, [MAKES SLIDE SOUND]. You see what I mean?
Now, with the advent of amplification and all that, then that was another ballgame. The guitar became prominent. Look at it today. You see what I mean?
Even in Merrie Old England, with the Beatles...
